title: Differentiable-plasticity coefficient bank
hypothesis: For aligned synthetic online learners, a shared Hebbian update basis plus compact task coordinates will preserve heldout adaptation while reducing serialized persistent and writable state relative to independent per-task plasticity tensors.
physical_object: Shared slow linear readout and Hebbian update basis
mirror_coordinate: Per-task coefficient vector over shared Hebbian update basis
controls: shared slow weights with fixed common Hebbian rule
independent full per-task update matrices upper control

development.selection_metric: heldout post-update prediction nRMSE subject to byte and update-MAC gates

success_gate: Mirror heldout nRMSE <= 0.02, at least 25% fewer total serialized bytes than independent coefficient bank, and online update MACs <= 1.25x independent; Mirror must beat native low-rank control by at least 10% bytes or 10% error.
failure_gate: Quality gate missed, byte saving <25%, update MAC >1.25x, or native low-rank matches Mirror within 1% bytes and error.
boundaries: Synthetic mechanism screen only; no trained differentiable-plasticity or language-model claim.
Persistent model bytes and writable per-episode fast-state bytes are reported separately and jointly.
Fresh seeds are evaluated after code/protocol freeze and never used to tune.
